t: Section 10216 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting after subsection (f) the following new subsection:“(g) Retention of Military Technicians Who Lose Dual Status Due to Combat-Related Disability.—(1) Notwithstanding subsection (d) of this section or subsections (a)(3) and (b) of section 10218 of this title, if a military technician (dual status) loses such dual status as the result of a combat-related disability (as defined in section 1413a of this title), the person may be retained as a non-dual status technician so long as—“(A) the combat-related disability does not prevent the person from performing the non-dual status functions or position; and“(B) the person, while a non-dual status technician, is not disqualified from performing the non-dual status functions or position because of performance, medical, or other reasons.“(2) A person so retained shall be removed not later than 30 days after becoming eligible for an unreduced annuity and becoming 60 years of age.“(3) Persons retained under the authority of this subsection do not count against the limitations of section 10217(c) of this title.”.

fable.w: This section only governs when the federal government may retain military technicians who lose dual status because of a combat-related disability; it is an internal federal personnel rule. The people affected are federal employees, and there is no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. Nothing here resembles participation beyond the fact that it concerns individuals' employment status.

It does not involve consultation with, or participation by, any party outside the federal government in a decision-making process. The interaction is strictly between the government and its employee regarding employment status.

opus.w: This section only sets the conditions for keeping or removing military technicians who are federal employees after a combat-related disability. It requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Reading the retention decision as participation is wrong because the only person involved is a federal employee, and no outside party has a role in the decision.
opus.s: if a military technician (dual status) loses such dual status as the result of a combat-related disability (as defined in section 1413a of this title), the person may be retained as a non-dual status technician
opus.b:
1. **Step 1:** One tempting reading is that letting a disabled technician be "retained" is a federal decision about someone outside the government. It isn't, because the technician is a federal employee. The section only covers that person's employment status: when they may be kept, when they must be removed, and how they count toward limits. No outside party is consulted, there is no hearing or comment period, and no outside party gets a right to sue.
